Item / what it does: Zone controller MCU (WiFi, ESPHome, local logic)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Genuine Espressif board, not a $3 clone. Enough GPIO for I2C + 1-Wire + 3 outputs. Clones use remarked modules, fake CP2102/CH340 USB chips and undersized AMS1117 regulators - the #1 cause of 'my node randomly reboots'. Base ESP32-C3-DEVKITM-1 is obsolete; buy the -N4X suffix.

Item / what it does: In-chamber RH + temperature sensor (Sensirion SHT41)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Sensirion die on a tested breakout with regulator + level shifting. Never buy a loose 'SHT40/SHT31 chip' from Amazon/AliExpress third parties - those are e-waste pulls or fakes. Tier 2 swaps this for the PTFE-filtered SHT45 (6174).

Item / what it does: Substrate core temperature probe, waterproof 1-Wire
Why this one / how not to get scammed: THE most counterfeited hobby sensor on earth. The $2 Amazon/AliExpress probes are usually clones that fail parasitic power, ignore resolution settings and read 2-4 C off. This is the authorized-channel version. Salt/ice test on arrival (see Scam checks).

Item / what it does: 5V 3A mains adapter, UL/ITE Class II, 2.1mm barrel
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Keeps 120VAC completely out of your enclosure - no mains copper on your custom PCB at all. Mean Well is heavily counterfeited on Amazon/eBay; buy from Digi-Key/Mouser/Newark/Arrow only.

Item / what it does: PCB-mount 2.1x5.5mm DC barrel jack
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Put a polyfuse + TVS diode right behind it on the PCB. Cheap generic jacks are fine - this is a 'bulk and dumb' part.

Item / what it does: I2C sensor cable, STEMMA QT / Qwiic, 100mm
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Keep I2C under ~30-50cm. Mount the node box right at the chamber wall and poke only the sensor through. Do NOT run I2C down metres of Cat5e (see Fixes tab).

Item / what it does: Gasketed ABS box for the brains, mounted OUTSIDE the chamber
Exact part number / SKU: Hammond 1591 series or hardware-store junction box
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Brains stay in dry air. Cheap box is genuinely fine here - that part of the advice was right. Add cable glands + a breather/desiccant. Tier 2 upgrades to IP68.

Item / what it does: IP68 cable glands, PG7/M12 assortment (20 pcs)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Truly un-fakeable. Gland every wire entry; drip-loop every cable so condensate runs away from the box, not into it.

Item / what it does: Louvered mist/radiation shield for the RH sensor
Exact part number / SKU: 3D print in PETG, or small vented box
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Sensor must see chamber air but never direct fog jet or dripping condensate. Point the sensor opening DOWN. Never conformal-coat the sensor opening.

Item / what it does: Pure-copper Cat6 patch cable, 10ft (1-Wire + logic runs)
Exact part number / SKU: Cat6 23/24AWG solid or stranded BARE COPPER, UL/ETL
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Scam: CCA (copper-clad aluminium) sold as Cat6. It is not compliant, corrodes at the punch-down and breaks 1-Wire. Scrape a conductor - silver core = CCA. Use one twisted pair per signal + its ground.

Item / what it does: Low-voltage fuse + holder (or PCB polyfuse)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: A shorted sensor wire in a wet chamber should blow a $0.30 part, not your ESP32 or the 5V supply.

Item / what it does: Output driver kit: 3x logic-level MOSFET + gate/pulldown resistors + flyback diodes
Why this one / how not to get scammed: An ESP32 GPIO is 3.3V; an Omron G3NA SSR input needs 5-24VDC. A 3.3V pin will not reliably trigger it. Low-side MOSFET per output lets 3.3V logic switch a 5V SSR/relay input, and the diode kills the coil kick. ~$0.50 of parts, buy 10.

Item / what it does: PCB connector set: 2x JST-PH 4-pin I2C + 6x 5.08mm screw terminals
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Screw terminals so you can swap a sensor without soldering inside a wet tent - the good idea from your advice. Phoenix if you want gas-tight clamps that survive humidity; generic 5.08mm is acceptable at these currents.

Item / what it does: Perfboard / Perma-Proto to run it before the PCB arrives
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Optional. Solder, don't breadboard - spring contacts oxidise in weeks at 95% RH. Excluded from tier totals.

Item / what it does: Silicone-modified conformal coating, 340g aerosol
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Cheaper at Altex ($39.99). Clean with IPA and dry FIRST; mask sensor opening, connectors, USB, buttons with Kapton. One can does dozens of boards. Acrylic (MG 419D) is easier to rework if you hate silicone.

Item / what it does: Kapton / polyimide masking tape, 12mm
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Masking is the whole game with conformal coating. Coating inside a connector = dead sensor bus.

Item / what it does: 99% isopropyl alcohol + acid brush
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Ionic flux residue + condensation = electrochemical migration (dendrites) even under coating. Clean before you coat.

Item / what it does: Adhesive-lined heat-shrink assortment
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Adhesive-lined (dual wall) only on the wet side. Plain shrink wicks moisture along the wire by capillary action.

Item / what it does: Silicone-insulated hook-up wire, 22AWG kit
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Flexible, heat tolerant, cheap. Buy from a seller that states copper strand count; CCA hook-up wire exists too.

Item / what it does: NEUTRAL-CURE RTV silicone sealant (non-corrosive)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: IMPORTANT FIX: ordinary '100% silicone' from the hardware store is usually ACETOXY cure - it releases acetic acid and eats copper and solder joints. Use neutral-cure (label says non-corrosive to metals / no vinegar smell).

Item / what it does: GFCI protection for every circuit feeding the chambers
Exact part number / SKU: Leviton GFNT1-W self-test receptacle or portable GFCI adapter
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Missing from the advice you were given, and the single most important item on this list. 100% RH + mains + water = GFCI is not optional. Test the trip button monthly.

Item / what it does: Custom carrier PCB, 3 copies, US-fabbed, no customs
Exact part number / SKU: OSH Park 2-layer, $5 per square inch (3 copies)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: $5/in^2 includes 3 boards + free US shipping. Keep the board <=5 in^2 (e.g. 2.0 x 2.5in) => ~$25. No tariff surprise, 9-12 days. Alternative: JLCPCB (see Tier 3 line) now lands at $30-60, not $2-5.

Item / what it does: Dashboard + logging host: Home Assistant + ESPHome + Grafana/InfluxDB
Exact part number / SKU: HA OS in Docker/VM on a PC you already own
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Free and local, as the advice said. Use an SSD, not an SD card - HA's database murders SD cards. Tier 2 buys a dedicated mini PC.

Item / what it does: Indicating silica-gel desiccant packs for the dry box
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Colour-change type so you can see saturation. Cheapest possible insurance for the brains.

Item / what it does: Mains switching with ZERO mains wiring: local smart plug + power metering
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Safest way to switch a humidifier/fan/heater: a listed enclosed device, no exposed 120V. Flash ESPHome (or use HA) for 100% local control. Power metering is your stuck-relay detector: if 'off' still draws 60W, alarm. Buy from the manufacturer's store, not a marketplace mystery seller.

Item / what it does: Sensor acceptance-test kit: saturated salt jar (75.3% RH @ 25C)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: How you catch a fake/drifted sensor in the first hour instead of after a lost crop. Saturated NaCl slurry = 75.3% RH. A 'Sensirion' reading 88% or 62% is a fake or damaged part - return it.

Item / what it does: Alternative plug: UL-certified, HA-native, no flashing needed
Why this one / how not to get scammed: UL certified, local Shelly integration in HA out of the box. If you specifically want ESPHome firmware, pick the older Plus Plug US or the S31 instead. Alternative to line 23, not additional.

Item / what it does: Alternative: enclosed logic-driven mains relay, 4 outlets
Exact part number / SKU: Digital Loggers IoT Power Relay II
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Opto-isolated 3-30V logic input, 2 NO + 2 NC outlets, fully enclosed and listed. Catch: ONE input switches ALL outlets, so it is 'fan+humidifier together', not independent loads. Great as a fail-safe (NC outlets drop out when the node asserts).

Item / what it does: UPGRADE delta: SHT41 -> SHT45 with PTFE filter (IP67)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Full price $13.50 (Jameco $17.65). Price shown is the DELTA over line 2 so totals don't double count - buy 6174 INSTEAD of 5776. 100um PTFE membrane, >99.99% filtration at 200nm, +/-1.0% RH, on-die heater to burn off condensation. This is the correct sensor for a spore-loaded, condensing chamber.

Item / what it does: CO2 sensor for fresh-air-exchange control (1 zone to start)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: CRITICAL: disable automatic self-calibration (ASC). ASC assumes the sensor sees 400ppm fresh air weekly; in a sealed fruiting chamber it will 'calibrate' your 8000ppm down to 400 and silently ruin your FAE logic. Use forced manual calibration outdoors instead.

Item / what it does: UPGRADE delta: IP68 / NEMA 6P polycarbonate enclosure
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Full price $38.99; delta over the $10 box in line 7. Buy this if the node must live inside the chamber/tent. Gasketed lid + glands + breather = genuinely survives fog.

Item / what it does: Independent hard-wired high-limit thermostat (backstop)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: THE fix for 'SSR fails closed'. Mechanical relay, its own probe, zero dependence on your ESP32 or WiFi. Set 3-5C above target; heater power flows THROUGH it. Also gives you high/low alarms. Cheap insurance for a heater that can cook a crop or start a fire.

Item / what it does: One-shot thermal cutoff bonded to the heater
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Last-ditch, physically bonded to the heater body, in series with the load. Pick a rating above your setpoint but below damage. Fuses do NOT protect against an SSR stuck on - this does.

Item / what it does: Spare sensor set (1x SHT41 + 1x DS18B20 probe)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Sensors are consumables in a fruiting chamber. A spare on the shelf turns a crop loss into a 5-minute swap. Also your known-good reference when a reading looks wrong.

Item / what it does: Dedicated always-on host: used mini PC, 8GB + SSD
Exact part number / SKU: Dell OptiPlex Micro / Lenovo Tiny / HP EliteDesk Mini
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Cheaper and far more durable than a Pi + SD card, and runs HA + InfluxDB + Grafana + ESPHome compiles comfortably. Buy a seller with a return policy; wipe and reinstall.

Item / what it does: Heater-only path: genuine SSR (instead of a smart plug)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: 10A, 24-240VAC, 5-24VDC input, zero-cross, UL/VDE. Buy ONLY from authorized distributors - 'Fotek/Omron' SSRs on marketplaces are the classic fire-starter fake. Needs a heatsink, leaks a few mA when 'off' (can keep a small humidifier trickling), and fails SHORT. Mandatory: series mechanical cutoff + thermal fuse + the Inkbird above.

Item / what it does: Heatsink for the SSR (required, not optional)
Exact part number / SKU: Omron Y92B-N50 or DIN heatsink <=1.5 C/W
Why this one / how not to get scammed: An SSR without a heatsink is a slow-motion failure. Thermal pad or paste, mounted vertically, in free air outside the tent.

Item / what it does: Loose genuine DS18B20 chips (DIY probes + authenticity reference)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Keep one known-genuine chip to compare scratchpad behaviour against suspect probes. Lasered marking + rear indent mark = genuine; printed marking = counterfeit.

Item / what it does: Premium in-chamber sensor: IP67 PTFE, replaceable pin connector
Why this one / how not to get scammed: +/-1.5% RH, PTFE membrane rated IP67, plugs into a 4-pin header so replacement needs no soldering inside a wet chamber. $33.64 at qty 5. Overkill vs the $13.50 SHT45+PTFE, but the most serviceable option.

Item / what it does: Rugged alternative: mesh-protected probe on 1m cable
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Sintered metal mesh + 1m cable, screw-mountable. Lower accuracy (+/-2% RH) than SHT45 but mechanically tough and already weatherproof - nice for a fog duct.

Item / what it does: Plug-and-play HA appliance instead of a mini PC
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Official price is $199 now - not the $99 it launched at. Only worth it if you want zero setup friction. A used mini PC gives more power for less.

Item / what it does: CO2 on every remaining zone (N-1 sensors)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Start with one, confirm your FAE logic, then scale. Excluded from totals because quantity depends on how many zones you instrument.

Item / what it does: More GPIO / PSRAM: S3 devkit instead of C3 (delta $7)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Only needed if you add a display, multiple 1-Wire buses, RS485 and camera-ish workloads. C3 is plenty for sensors + relays.

Item / what it does: China fab path: 5 bare PCBs, landed cost with 2026 tariffs
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Boards are still ~$2-8, but JLC now pre-collects US import fees (their Oct 2026 table: ~35-92.5% total) plus $15-35 shipping. Real-world landed reports: $30-60. The '$2-5 total for 5 boards' in your advice is years out of date.

Item / what it does: Turnkey assembled boards (5 pcs, landed)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Real-world report: $25 boards+stencil, $25 tariff, $35 shipping = ~$80. Worth it once your design is frozen; not for rev A.

Item / what it does: Industrial panel option: DIN rail + enclosed PSU + contactor
Exact part number / SKU: Mean Well HDR-15-5 + Phoenix 1757242 terminals + DIN contactor
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Only if you want a proper wired panel with a mechanical contactor in series with the SSR. Have mains work done by someone qualified; keep the panel outside the wet space.

Item / what it does: Wired backhaul if WiFi is unreliable in a metal room
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Isolated PoE variant - do not use the non-isolated board near mains. Alternative to WiFi per node; still keep I2C short.

Item / what it does: Temperature-controlled soldering iron
Why this one / how not to get scammed: A cold joint is a humidity failure waiting to happen. Anything temperature-controlled beats a $12 firestick.

Item / what it does: Multimeter for commissioning
Why this one / how not to get scammed: You need continuity + DC volts + AC volts to prove the safety chain works before you trust it.

Item / what it does: USB power meter (node current / brownout diagnosis)
Why this one / how not to get scammed: Cheap way to prove your 5V rail isn't sagging when the relay pulls in.
